entries.title: Sam Rinzel's monster game lifts Blackhawks to dramatic first road win
entries.summary: <p>CALGARY, Alberta — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> defenseman Sam Rinzel had no words Saturday night to describe what he had just done.</p><p>"I don’t know," Rinzel said, chuckling. "Credit to my teammates, for sure. I’m just playing hockey. I don’t really know. It’s just [about] getting back to not thinking and just playing."</p><p>Rinzel's game-winning goal with 14 seconds left in overtime — he chipped a loose puck over Flames goalie Dustin Wolf to give the Hawks a 4-3 win, their long-awaited first road victory of the season — capped a ridiculous individual performance and extended a ridiculous individual heater.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Sam Rinzel caps off a signature game with the OT winner. He’s on a ridiculous heater <a href="https://t.co/ImRY8AKWyq">pic.twitter.com/ImRY8AKWyq</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2124283576753717706?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 21, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Even before that goal, the suddenly blossoming 22-year-old Minnesota product had already tallied two assists, becoming the first Hawks defenseman to record five consecutive multi-point games since Pierre Pilote in 1962. He also became just the fourth defenseman in NHL history to record five consecutive multi-assist games.</p><p>"That's pretty cool for him," coach Jeff Blashill said. "He's definitely playing with much more swagger, similar probably to the way he would've in college and junior. Hopefully, it's really starting to click for him. You're not going to keep this pace up, but just his overall game has been pretty consistent."</p><p>Rinzel also saved the Hawks from doom in the final minute of regulation by denying a Matt Coronato wrap-around shot. He displayed tremendous strength to hold his stick on the goal line with the puck pushing against it.</p><p>"I just tried to put my bottom hand low and just squeeze the heck out of it," Rinzel said.</p><p>After struggling pretty heartily throughout the first month of the season, Rinzel's sudden transformation into unstoppable force is an exciting development. He's up to 17 points in 22 games, which ranks among the top 20 defensemen NHL-wide.</p><p>"I'm just not afraid to just play. Don't think, just play," he said. "I still make a lot of mistakes now, don't get me wrong. There's still a lot of stuff to clean up. But [I] just go play."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">This required some serious hand strength by Rinzel: <a href="https://t.co/7bYQkXajEG">pic.twitter.com/7bYQkXajEG</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2124280155338363220?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 21, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>Kaiser ejected</b></h3><p>Hawks defenseman Wyatt Kaiser was ejected for a high hit on Flames forward Martin Pospisil during the second period, giving the hosts a lengthy power play during which they eventually tied the game.</p><p>The Hawks have a history of animosity with Pospisil, who took cheap shots on each of Connor Bedard, Frank Nazar and Taylor Hall back in 2024-25. But Kaiser insisted there was nothing personal behind the hit, and Blashill backed his claim.</p><p>"I didn’t know [it was Pospisil] until I hit him, really," Kaiser said. "I just had a good gap coming in. I was like, 'OK, I can push this.' Saw the pull-drag and went for the hit."</p><p>Said Blashill: "It was no ill intention from Kaiser's part whatsoever. He's not that kind of player, never has been. He was trying to make a hit. It was too bad because I thought Kais was playing excellent."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Kaiser ejected for this hit on Pospisil, who has taken some cheap shots on Hawks over the years: <a href="https://t.co/LvuVqvH78D">pic.twitter.com/LvuVqvH78D</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2124264480054071435?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 21, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Down to five defensemen, Blashill leaned heavily on Rinzel and Alex Vlasic. The former ended up logging more than 26 minutes and the latter more than 28 minutes.</p><p>The NHL will surely take a look at the hit, and there's a decent chance Kaiser could face suspension. That could then force the Hawks to move Kevin Korchinski back into their lineup Sunday against the Canucks.</p><h3><b>Kane scored</b></h3><p>Rinzel's second assist set up Patrick Kane for a blistering one-timer on a power play, which finally snapped Kane's goal drought that stretched back to the season opener.</p><p>"Hopefully, I’ll get hot now," Kane said. "It'll be nice."</p>

entries.title: Mount Carmel handles Oswego, heads to fifth consecutive state championship game
entries.summary: <p>All season long, the headlines have gone to Mount Carmel’s high-powered offense, which is fueled by the best receiving duo in the state in Marshaun Thornton and Quentin Burrell.</p><p>But as the Caravan head back downstate next weekend in pursuit of their fifth consecutive state title and record 18th overall, give a thought to their defense.</p><p>Led by top prospects Darin Graham and Caleb Tucker, No. 2 Mount Carmel shut down No. 4 Oswego after halftime to pull away for a 38-18 home victory in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/11/20/2026-ihsa-state-football-semifinal-scores" target="_blank" >Class 8A semifinals</a> Saturday.</p><p>The Caravan (11-2) will play New Trier or St. Ignatius for the 8A title at 7 p.m. next Saturday at Illinois State’s Hancock Stadium.</p><p>Graham, a 6-5, 224-pounder, had two sacks in the third quarter, including a strip sack and fumble recovery on the Panthers’ first possession of the second half. Tucker also had a sack in that quarter as Mount Carmel scored twice to turn a 17-10 halftime lead into a 31-10 advantage.</p><p>‘‘I feel like the week of practice we had was tremendous,’’ Graham said. ‘‘We had a lot going into this game. We definitely didn’t like how we played last week [in a 21-16 victory against Lincoln-Way East], so we knew we had to bring the energy. Me and my D-line, we knew we had to play better. It was either win or go home.’’</p><p>Oswego (11-2), which lost to the Caravan in the 8A title game last season, has some dynamic playmakers in running back Ammar Banire and dual-threat quarterback Drew Kleinhans. But Mount Carmel held Banire to 41 yards on 19 rushes and limited Kleinhans to 93 total yards before he left with a shoulder injury after Graham’s second sack.</p><p>‘‘He’s a senior,’’ Caravan coach Jordan Lynch said of Graham, who committed to Ohio this month. ‘‘He plays hard, he plays fast, plays relentless. And we’re only going to go as far as our seniors take us.’’</p><p>Tucker said he wasn’t surprised to see Graham make some big plays.</p><p>‘‘That’s one of my favorite seniors,’’ Tucker said. ‘‘We grew up in the same area. He’s really got that dog in him. He’s striving for greatness, and I love that about him.’’</p><p>Mount Carmel’s offense made its usual share of big plays. Brady Cloherty had touchdown passes of 64 and 30 yards to four-star junior Thornton and also ran for a score.</p><p>‘‘You’ve always got to set the tone,’’ Thornton said of his 64-yard touchdown, which put the Caravan ahead to stay. ‘‘I’m a big player, so I’ve got to make big-time plays.’’</p><p>Cloherty has thrown 50 touchdown passes this season, a program record and the eighth-best single-season total in state history, according to the IHSA website. Against Oswego, he was 10-for-24 for 201 yards with two interceptions. Thornton had four catches for 113 yards, and Nathan Samuels and Duran Sims also ran for touchdowns.</p><p>Kleinhans threw a touchdown pass to Graham Schwab and Cam Loghmani returned a punt for a score for the Panthers.</p><p>‘‘You might say their kids are faster and their kids are bigger . . . but [it was] a typical Panther football showing,’’ Oswego coach Brian Cooney said. ‘‘I know the scoreboard didn’t go the way we wanted. But, man, our kids will put their hand in the dirt and play football with anyone, anywhere, and I’m really proud of how they played.’’</p>

entries.title: Katin Houser throws for 318 yards, but Illini still fall to Hawkeyes
entries.summary: <p>CHAMPAIGN — L.J. Phillips Jr. ran for 154 yards and a touchdown, Iowa's stingy defense shut out Illinois in the second half, and the No. 13 Hawkeyes beat the Fighting Illini 34-17 on Saturday to give their College Football Playoff hopes a big boost.</p><p>Phillips went over 100 yards rushing for the third straight game, Xavier Williams added 59 yards rushing and a score, and Hank Brown ran for 32 yards and another TD, as the Hawkeyes (9-2, 6-2 Big Ten) outgained Illinois 264-28 on the ground.</p><p>Brown also was 13 of 26 for 138 yards through the air, helping the Hawkeyes to their fourth consecutive win.</p><p>As for the playoffs, where Iowa was 15th in the latest rankings released by the selection committee?</p><p>“I could care less about those guys. They're going to do what they're going to do," Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz said. “Our goal was to come in here and get a win. It's not easy to win in college football. It's not easy to win a conference game on the road.</p><p>"I'm real happy for our guys.”</p><p>Katin Houser threw for 318 yards with two touchdown passes and two interceptions for Illinois (6-5, 4-4), which lost its second in a row after a four-game winning streak. Collin Dixon caught eight passes for 142 yards while Brayden Trimble had four catches for 121 yards and a touchdown.</p><p>The Hawkeyes put the game away midway through the fourth quarter with a grinding, 19-play, 91-yard drive that took 10 minutes off the clock. It ended when Brown scored from 2 yards out on a fourth-down draw play to put Iowa in front 27-17.</p><p>“Classic Iowa,” said Illini coach Bret Bielema, who played for the Hawkeyes from 1989-92. “Just kept doing enough to get a first down here, a first down there.</p><p>“They're the most complete team we've played all year," Bielema added. "They can beat anyone in the country."</p><p>Jaylen Watson added a 40-yard interception return for a touchdown about four minutes after Brown's TD for the final margin.</p><p>The Fighting Illini punted three times in the third quarter, including a pair of three-and-outs, and were stopped on fourth down twice along with the interception in the fourth.</p><p>That came after the game was tied 17-17 at halftime.</p><p>Houser threw a 75-yard touchdown pass to Trimble and an 11-yard TD pass to Davin Stoffel. Trimble tip-toed along the sideline after catching a short pass before being sprung by a block by fellow wide receiver Eddie Kasper.</p><p>Iowa scored on 2-yard runs by Phillips and Williams. An interception by Cam Buffington on a dropped pass set up Williams’ score.</p><h3><b>The takeaway</b></h3><p>Iowa: The nation’s No. 1 scoring defense rose to the occasion in the second half against Illinois, which managed more points in the first half against the Hawkeyes than any of their previous four opponents had managed in an entire game.</p><p>Illinois: Injuries have been a major storyline for the Illini offense. Houser has continued to play despite a broken hand and broken nose and No. 2 receiver Hudson Clement is out for the season, as are top running backs Ca’Lil Valentine and Javari Barnett.</p><h3><b>Iowa’s recent domination</b></h3><p>The Hawkeyes have won 15 of the last 17 against Illinois and 18 of the last 22 in the series, dating back to 1996. Ferentz is now 15-4 against the Illini, while the series going back to the first meeting in 1899 is tied 39-39-2.</p><h3><b>Up next </b></h3><p>Iowa hosts Nebraska on Friday in what is known as the Heroes Game.</p><p>Illinois plays at Northwestern next Saturday.</p>

entries.title: Connor Bedard to undergo shoulder surgery this week
entries.summary: <p>CALGARY, Alberta — Connor Bedard will undergo surgery on his right shoulder this week, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> general manager Kyle Davidson said Saturday.</p><p>This comes less than five months after Bedard had surgery on his left shoulder. </p><p>It will "likely" be the exact same surgery, Davidson said, and it will be conducted by the same Colorado-based surgeon, Dr. Peter Millett. He has a lengthy history of successful surgeries on NHL players.</p><p>Bedard suffered this new right-shoulder injury Tuesday against the Maple Leafs and spent the last few days deciding whether to get surgery or try to return through rehab alone.</p><p>A return timeline will be determined after the surgery, Davidson said. Bedard was initially estimated to miss four months after his July surgery but returned after three months. Three months from now is late February. </p><p>Davidson said any conversations about Bedard potentially returning this season will be had "at a later date." But it's safe to assume he will miss at least the majority of it.</p><p>"We’ll work with Connor," Davidson said. "He has unfortunately been through this not in the too-distant past, so he knows the drill and knows what he needs to do. We know he’s going to attack this recovery the same way he has with his other one, and [we] expect it to go very well."</p><p>Davidson said the Hawks are confident Bedard will be able to resume playing center and taking faceoffs in the future — even though both of his right-shoulder injuries (on Tuesday and last December) occurred on faceoffs.</p><p>Surgically repaired shoulders generally aren't as strong as normal, never-injured shoulders, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/19/blackhawks-connor-bedard-injury-surgery-rehab-decision" >according</a> to Dr. Jorge Chahla of Rush University. To be fair, though, Bedard's left shoulder has seemingly held up well since Millett repaired it.</p><p>"Once these surgeries are done, they have a high success rate," Davidson said. "He’s getting the best treatment. He’s getting the best people. And we know that when he is given a task...he’s going to do everything in his power to make sure it’s a successful recovery. So we have all the confidence in the world that this is going to go the way we all want it to."</p><p>Davidson also said Bedard's injury doesn't change his intention to improve the Hawks' current roster via trades, noting that "nothing has changed with our asset base."</p><p>He also wants the guys currently in the lineup to "keep taking steps," obviously. But injuries are mounting throughout the roster. </p><p>Defenseman Bowen Byram, who hasn't played since Oct. 13 due to a finicky upper-body injury, didn't travel with the Hawks for their 4-3 overtime win Saturday at the Flames. Byram won't play Sunday against the Canucks and is "doubtful" to join the team before they face the Kraken on Wednesday, coach Jeff Blashill said. Neither Blashill nor Davidson had updates beyond that.</p><p>Center Anton Frondell left the game Saturday with a new injury unrelated to the nagging injury he was already dealing with, Blashill said. His status is now uncertain, too.</p><p>These newly created holes could add extra vigor to Davidson's scouring of the trade market, which he described as "relentless."</p><p>"When you drop bodies, you have the avenue of recalls," he said. "But at some point, you don’t want to keep exhausting and moving players up the chain over and over and over again, because then you start running out of players organizationally. We want to maybe safeguard [against] that."</p><p>Davidson acknowledged, though, that players utilizing no-trade clauses to block moves to Chicago is an inevitable challenge of their situation.</p><p>"Our record is not one that we’ve earned the benefit of the doubt," he said. "It’s up to us and the players to change the narrative there. ... When you are where we are in the standings, that’s what comes with the territory. I don’t care how good your city is, people get in this business to win."</p>

entries.title: Brother Rice dominates East St. Louis to earn a return trip to the 7A title game
entries.summary: <p>East St. Louis, one of the state’s great high school football programs, is accustomed to physically dominating opponents. The Flyers are usually bigger and faster.</p><p>Saturday on the Southwest Side, East St. Louis more than met its match. Brother Rice’s defense dominated the Flyers in a 24-12 win in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/11/20/2026-ihsa-state-football-semifinal-scores" >Class 7A semifinals</a>, led by defensive linemen Kam McGee, Braydon Parks, Tymel Lofton and Nathan Elsea.</p><p>“We couldn’t run the ball,” East St. Louis coach Darren Sunkett said. “We didn’t have time to throw the ball. They were as good as advertised up front. They just kicked our [butts] for four quarters up front.”</p><p>The Crusaders (11-2) won 7A last year and will face undefeated Hersey in the championship on Saturday at ISU’s Hancock Stadium.</p><p>“We just had to be physical,” Parks said. “They are going to come in and do their thing. We weren’t afraid of that and played our football.”</p><p>East St. Louis (11-2) had 0 total rushing yards on 20 carries. Quarterback Reece Shanklin was sacked five times and finished with 10 carries for -50 yards.</p><p>“All week we talked about explosiveness and getting off the ball,” Lofton said.</p><p>McGee, a junior, is one of the best players in the country. Parks is a senior heading to Notre Dame, but Lofton is relatively unknown.</p><p>“[Lofton] has had a fantastic year,” Brother Rice coach Casey Quedenfeld said. “The amount of hustle and effort plays he has made downfield, in addition to the sacks and hurries. He’s fantastic; today there were just reporters here to see it.”</p><p>Brother Rice sucked up as much clock as possible on each offensive drive. Freshman quarterback Sam Holcomb had 20 carries for 86 yards and a touchdown, and running back Jameson Davis finished with 12 carries for 65 yards. The totals aren’t gaudy, but both players picked up big gains in key moments and often took a punishing hit at the end of the run.</p><p>“[East St. Louis] is extremely fast in the back end and they do a great job of coming downhill and being reckless, in a good way, and of tackling,” Quedenfeld said. “We talked all week about protecting yourself because there were going to be big impacts.”</p><p>Holcomb was 7-for-12 passing for 40 yards with two touchdowns and one interception. entries.title: Teen critically wounded in Riverdale shooting
entries.summary: <p>An 18-year-old was critically wounded in a shooting late Saturday in Riverdale on the Far South Side, police said. </p><p>The teen was standing outside a courtyard in the 800 block of East 130th Place around 7:41 p.m. when he was approached several men. One of them, who was armed, shot him in the head, police said. He was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center in critical condition.</p><p>The men fled the scene on foot, according to police. Area 2 detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: An e-scooter law in Illinois takes effect Jan. 1. How it aims to make riding them safer
entries.summary: <p>This year, several people in Chicago have <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/05/01/loved-ones-launch-fundraiser-for-venezuelan-teenager-killed-in-south-side-scooter-crash" target="_blank" >died</a> while riding e-scooters, including <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/04/alex-blacio-scooter-death-western" target="_blank" ><u>teenagers</u></a>. </p><p>This month alone, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/11/06/electric-scooter-driver-67-killed-in-collision-with-speeding-suv-in-north-park" target="_blank" ><u>two men</u></a>, ages 67 and 39, were killed in collisions with vehicles. Hundreds in Chicago have been <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/transportation/2026/06/05/scooter-teen-crash-death-lane-tech-high-school-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>injured</u></a> in e-scooter accidents in the past few years as ridership grows. A new Illinois law aims to make riding e-scooters and e-bikes safer.</p><h3><b>What’s the new Illinois e-scooter law that goes into effect Jan. 1?</b></h3><p>The law classifies any device capable of going faster than 28 mph as motor vehicles and subjects their operators to the state’s drunken driving laws, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/06/04/e-bike-moto-regulation-illinois-pritzker-giannoulias" target="_blank" ><u>Sun-Times reported</u></a>. Legislation passed in June and was signed by Gov. JB Pritzker in August. It seeks to address a rise in injuries among children using them.</p><p>Owners of those high-speed devices — which can include e-bikes, e-motos, e-scooters, electric unicycles, electric skateboards — will be required to have a driver’s license, carry insurance and register their vehicle with the state. They will not be allowed on bike paths and, in some cases, bike lanes.</p><p>The law creates consistent rules for the devices across the state, eliminating a growing and inconsistent patchwork of local ordinances.</p><h3><b>Are there age minimums for riders of e-scooters and e-bikes?</b></h3><p>Yes. The law strengthens existing age minimums for e-bike and e-scooter riders.</p><p>Class 1 and Class 2 e-bikes, which go up to 20 mph, must be operated by someone at least 15 years old, according to the law. Riders must be at least 16 years old for Class 3 e-bikes, which go up to 28 mph. E-scooter users must be at least 16 years old, and are capped at 15 mph.</p><p>Though Lime and Divvy require riders to be 18 or older — or at least 16 with parental consent — younger riders are still using them. An evaluation of the city’s 2020 e-scooter pilot program found that minors accounted for roughly 13% of reported injuries.</p><p>There are ways underage riders can get access to e-scooters, such as using an <a class="Link" href="https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/cost-our-family-everything-parents-sound-alarm-after-teen-deaths-on-e-scooters/3942060/" target="_blank" ><u>adult’s account</u></a>, though the <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicago.gov/content/dam/city/depts/cdot/Misc/EScooters/2022/Chicago%20Scooter%20License%20Rules%20and%20Regulations%20-%20Final%20Draft%20Signed.pdf" target="_blank" >city’s own ordinance </a>says that minors need permission from a parent or guardian to use the devices. The new state law, however, does not mandate e-scooter vendors strengthen ID verification requirements. </p><p><a class="Link" href="https://news.wttw.com/2026/08/18/e-scooter-safety-concerns-rise-chicago-sees-record-high-ridership" target="_blank" >Divvy told WTTW</a> in August that underage riders are banned immediately if caught operating an e-scooter without adult consent. Lime rolled out an <a class="Link" href="https://www.li.me/blog/keeping-dc-moving-lime-invests-17-million-in-capitals-thriving-micromobility-program" target="_blank" >AI verification system</a> in Washington, D.C. that can identify underage riders who make require another layer of identification. </p><h3><b>Are e-scooter accidents increasing?</b></h3><p>Yes. The Chicago Fire Department responded to nearly 200 e-scooter-related incidents in 2022. Within three years, that number had more than tripled, <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/transportation/2026/06/05/scooter-teen-crash-death-lane-tech-high-school-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>WBEZ reported</u></a>.</p><p>One national study found a 7.5-fold <a class="Link" href="https://www.usatoday.com/story/graphics/2026/07/29/e-bike-injuries-child-kids-safety-health-transit/90956259007/" target="_blank" ><u>increase</u></a> in children on the vehicles seeking emergency care from 2023 to 2026.</p><p>But their popularity among teens — who are at times under the legal riding age — is growing as the city sees a rise in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2024/10/09/lime-divvy-chicago-e-scooter-riders-serious-injuries" target="_blank" >scooter-related crashes</a>, raising <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/05/04/chicago-launches-e-scooter-safety-campaign-in-wake-of-recent-scooter-deaths" target="_blank" >safety concerns</a> among doctors and city officials</p><h3><b>Has e-scooter ridership grown in Chicago?</b></h3><p>Yes. Chicago launched its first <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2019/6/11/18661876/electric-scooters-chicago-10-vendors-bird-bolt-gruv-jump-lime-lyft-sherpa-spin-veoride-wheels" target="_blank" >e-scooter pilot program</a> in 2019. By 2022, Lime and Divvy e-scooters became ubiquitous.</p><p>Lime, which is partially owned by Uber, has grown from operating 1,000 scooters in 2022 to 11,000 as of this past summer, according to <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/transportation/2026/06/05/scooter-teen-crash-death-lane-tech-high-school-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>WBEZ</u></a>. Divvy, operated by Lyft, has expanded its fleet to 2,800 e-scooters.</p><p>Combined, e-scooter ridership for these two companies totaled almost 7 million trips last year, according to the Chicago Department of Transportation.</p><p>More than 3.7 million trips were recorded on rental e-scooters between mid-2022 and late 2023, according to city data, compared with 1.3 million rides between 2019 and 2020, reported the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2024/10/09/lime-divvy-chicago-e-scooter-riders-serious-injuries" target="_blank" ><u>Sun-Times</u></a>.</p><h3><b>What is Chicago doing to make riding e-scooters safer?</b></h3><p>In May, the city of Chicago launched an e-scooter <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/05/04/chicago-launches-e-scooter-safety-campaign-in-wake-of-recent-scooter-deaths" target="_blank" ><u>safety campaign</u></a>. It included new rider safety messaging across the city and expanded scooter parking and bike infrastructure. The campaign also included stronger compliance requirements for operators and riders that will include stronger parking standards and expanded sidewalk-riding detection technology.</p>

entries.title: Notre Dame defense stifles SMU in 24-3 victory
entries.summary: <p>SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Notre Dame’s defense held SMU to its lowest point total since 2016, and the No. 3 Fighting Irish ground out a 24-3 victory on Saturday night.</p><p>It was SMU’s lowest point total since a 33-3 loss to TCU in September 2016.</p><p>Notre Dame (10-1) stopped six SMU drives inside Fighting Irish territory. Notre Dame turned the Mustangs (7-4) over three times on downs, at the 19, the 2 and the 3.</p><p>After rolling up a streak of 126 consecutive games scoring in double-digits, SMU has now suffered back-to-back losses scoring less than 10 points. The Mustangs were defeated 49-7 last week by No. 10 Wake Forest.</p><p>“It’s been an area of focus, especially since the bye week,” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman said of playing tough in the red zone. "We recognized that was an area we have to get better at. We tried to be intentional about the work we put in.</p><p>“They played well,” Freeman added about the defense. “They played with clarity. They played — on their side of the line of scrimmage, I thought our D-line did a really good job, and then they matched up in coverage.”</p><p>Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr completed 19 of 29 passes for 312 yards and a TD.</p><p>SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings was 24 of 45 for 216 yards.</p><p>Notre Dame linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa said that the Fighting Irish defense has a fierce mindset.</p><p>“We talk about planting the flag,” Viliamu-Asa. “It’s a four-point battle, assuming they’re going to get three points out of it. When you get in the red zone, what really helps is everybody doing their job, having good eyes, having good communication."</p><p>Viliamu-Asa said that keeping Jennings from having chances for explosive plays was a point of emphasis.</p><p>“He’s a great quarterback with a lot of experience,” Viliamu-Asa said. “The game plan was just get in his face, everybody do their job, and when we get a chance to hit him, hit him. When we get a chance to get him off his platform, go get his (butt).”</p><p>SMU coach Rhett Lashlee said that Jennings rolled his ankle in the second quarter, which affected his mobility.</p><p>Lashlee was disappointed his team couldn’t cash in on opportunities.</p><p>“We did a lot of things to give ourselves a chance,” Lashlee said. “0h-and-3 in the red zone is why it’s not 24-17 late with us driving to try and tie the game. They’re really good, so give them credit. We did a lot of things that would have told you we’d have a chance in the fourth quarter, but not finishing a couple of drives inside the 10 did not allow us to have that chance."</p><p>Notre Dame forged a 17-3 halftime lead with a couple of spectacular plays.</p><p>Jordan Faison made a one-handed grab in the end zone for a 21-yard touchdown from Carr that gave Notre Dame a 14-3 lead.</p><p>SMU drove to the Notre Dame 24, but a leaping interception in the end zone by Jayden Sanders stopped the Mustangs late in the second quarter.</p><p><b>Talich and Greathouse injured</b></p><p>Notre Dame lost two impact players to injuries in the first half.</p><p>Defensive back Luke Talich, who leads the Fighting Irish with three interceptions, suffered an injury after breaking up a pass in the end zone that stopped an early SMU threat. Talich returned to the sidelines on crutches later in the first half.</p><p>Greathouse, a wide receiver who has two touchdowns and averages 14.2 yards a catch, left the game after making a catch for a 62-yard gain that led to Notre Dame’s first touchdown. He was ruled out for the rest of the game with an undisclosed injury.</p><p><b>The takeaway</b></p><p>Notre Dame: Although the Fighting Irish didn’t pile up style points in the victory against SMU, UCLA’s loss could help Notre Dame move up in the College Football Playoff rankings. The Irish can lock up a spot in the College Football Playoff next week. They were sixth in this week’s rankings.</p><p>SMU: The Mustangs are 0-3 vs. ranked opponents this season, losing to No. 23 Louisville 41-13, No. 11 Wake Forest 49-7, and No. 3 Notre Dame 24-3.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Notre Dame visits Syracuse on Saturday.</p><p>SMU visits Stanford on Saturday.</p>

entries.title: Man found dead at CTA Red Line station amid North Side shootings had self-inflicted gunshot wound
entries.summary: <p>A man found dead at a CTA Red Line station tied to a string of recent shootings on the North Side had a self-inflicted gunshot wound. </p><p>Detectives have linked two recent fatal shootings in Rogers Park to a robbery and shooting in Lake View that occurred Wednesday and Thursday, Chicago police said. </p><p>Police initially described the deceased man — found early Thursday in the stairwell of the CTA Red Line's Morse station at 1358 W. Morse Ave., — as 25 years old. The Cook County medical examiner's office later determined Friday he was 19 and ruled his death a suicide. His name has not been released.</p><p>The first shooting occurred about 10:40 p.m. Wednesday when a 35-year-old man who had been robbed was found wounded along a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/11/19/man-shot-robbed-lake-view-bike-path" target="_blank" >bike path in the 3300 block of North DuSable</a> Lake Shore Drive in Lake View.</p><p>Then, at 11:15 p.m., <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/11/19/woman-fatally-shot-during-homicide-man-fatally-shot-in-death-investigation-overnight-in-rogers-park" target="_blank" >24-year-old Bintou Salami</a> was found with a fatal gunshot wound to her head outside her apartment in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue in Rogers Park.</p><p>Salami, who recently moved to the neighborhood to be closer to her job at Misericordia Heart of Mercy, was parking a Lime scooter when someone attempted to rob her before being shot, Salami’s family told the Chicago Sun-Times.</p><p>Salami's brother, Raoufou, has since organized a <a class="Link" href="https://www.gofundme.com/f/help-lay-bintou-salami-to-rest" target="_blank" >GoFundMe</a> to help with funeral expenses and to "ease some of the burden" for her loved ones in the wake of her death, he wrote. She leaves behind a son in her home country of Togo, Africa, according to the post. </p><p>The crowdfunding effort has raised $35,000 toward a $50,000 goal as of Saturday night. </p><p>Two hours later and about half-mile away from Salami's slaying, a man was found with a fatal gunshot wound to the head at the Red Line Morse station.</p><p>Police have not provided a description of a suspect or confirmed that investigators are seeking an assailant in connection with the attacks. No one was in custody.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Education is the best weapon against online dangers
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My 70-year-old brother, "Ardal," called me recently, and I'm still reeling from what he said. He was scammed out of $30,000. Ardal has never been tech-savvy, and he lives a simple life. Even so, the extent of his gullibility is astounding. These thieves knew exactly what to say to allay his suspicions. He literally handed over a bag of $30,000 in cash to a stranger in order to "protect" the rest of his financial assets and "prevent the FBI from arresting him." Only when the thieves requested an additional $20,000 did my brother finally get wise and go to the police.</p><p>The whole thing started when Ardal opened an email he should have deleted. Please advise your readers that these scams are real, and the thieves are on the lookout for naive and trusting people like my brother to prey on. My best piece of advice: If you click on a link and believe you've downloaded malware, unplug your computer and take it to a reputable shop. — <i>SAD SISTER</i></p><p><b>DEAR SISTER:</b> Thank you for your cautionary tale. Readers, if you use a computer for any reason — even if it's for nothing more than email — it's imperative that you get training on internet safety. Check with your community centers, senior centers, employers and schools to learn how to prevent this kind of disaster from affecting you.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I have a friend of 40 years. We raised our kids together, planned weddings, welcomed each other's grandchildren and went on vacations together for years. Her youngest granddaughter was born two years ago, and they live several states away, so we didn't meet the child until they all gathered for a camping trip near us this past summer. We went to visit them there for the day.</p><p>When we arrived and met the little girl, I realized that she had some challenges. She did not walk or talk. I suspect that she has cerebral palsy. My friend never said anything about this to me, either before the visit or after.</p><p>I was perplexed by the situation and still don't know if I should say or ask anything. I am hurt that she never said a thing about the complications they have all been dealing with. Should I say anything or remain silent if or until she mentions it? — <i>DIDN'T KNOW IN NEW YORK</i></p><p><b>DEAR DIDN'T KNOW:</b> Stop feeling hurt. Your friend may not have discussed the child's developmental issues with you because the subject is painful for them. Although your intentions are good, I hope you will not bring it up.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My daughter forgot my 75th birthday, and I feel so hurt. I don't know what to say to her. She's the mother of two teenage boys and is quite busy. I didn't expect any gifts and certainly not a party, but I did expect some acknowledgement. What do I say if and when she finally remembers? — <i>FORGOTTEN IN NEW MEXICO</i></p><p><b>DEAR FORGOTTEN:</b> What you should say is, "Thank you. How sweet of you." Period. When she finally remembers, she will already feel terrible without any admonishment from you.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127. </p>

entries.title: Review: “Home, I’m Darling” at TimeLine Theatre Co.
entries.summary: <p>Is it crazy to want to live a life out of the past when, at least in your mind, things were simpler? When people paid more attention to each other rather than their cell phones, when appliances were built to last and clothing was made with hand-crafted details? When, rather than the modern rush, you had time to grow all your own vegetables, make dinner every night, spend lingering evenings with friends?</p><p>British playwright Laura Wade’s intriguingly complex dramedy “Home, I’m Darling,” receiving its Chicago premiere at TimeLine Theatre, contemplates nostalgia taken to its most extreme, and, perhaps as expected, mostly imploding.</p><p>The opening scene shows us a world out of 1950s television perfection. Meticulously-coiffed housewife Judy (Claire Kaplan) joyfully prepares her husband Johnny’s (Elliot Sagay) breakfast. Over apparently transcendent toast and homemade marmalade, they chat about how blissfully content they are: “appallingly happy,” Johnny insists.</p><div class="RatingCard Enhancement" data-module data-rating="3.0" data-align-center> <div class="RatingCard-title"> “Home, I’m Darling” </div> <div class="RatingCard-content"> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> </div> </div><p></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-2a0000" name="module-2a0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><b>When</b>: Through Dec. 13<br><b>Where</b>: TimeLine Theatre Co. (5035 N. Broadway.)<br><b>Info</b>: <a class="Link" href="https://timelinetheatre.com/events/home-darling/" target="_blank" ><u>Tickets</u></a> from $40; run time is 2 hour and 25 minutes with one intermission</div> </div><p>After he leaves for work, lunchbox and briefcase in hand, the wife sits down at the kitchen table and pulls out her laptop.</p><p>Judy wants to live in the ‘50s, or at least her idealized version<i> </i>of them. After getting laid off from her job in finance, she implored and convinced Johnny to give that a genuine shot, even though it’s the 21st century (the play was written in 2018 and won London’s Olivier Award for Best New Comedy). The laptop? Well, it’s simply a necessary exception to source all those vintage items for their home décor and wardrobe. It’s also very useful for finding the like-minded.</p><p>Once we discover the concept, some predictable conflicts arise. Judy’s mother, the practical and mildly bohemian Sylvia (Janet Ulrich Brooks), who unlike Judy <i>lived</i> through the ‘50s, vociferously disapproves of trying to re-create an era she and other women worked hard to revolutionize. They’re tempted to enter this way of living themselves, but we begin to wonder whether that’s mostly just because Fran loves the clothes and wishes her house was cleaner and Marcus wishes… Well, let’s just say the ‘50s norms had many advantages for men — at least for white men — the lack of certain employment laws being one of them. English manners had, and still have, an even heavier, obligatory refinement. Wade is clearly a stickler for language, and although the accents here are all strong enough and the actors gifted, the rhythm of the dialogue, the placement and length of ripe pauses, require more surgical precision to hit their full effect. You can tell because sometimes they <i>do </i>work completely, particularly when Rowe is involved.</p><p>But even when not hitting all its moments, this production sure serves as pleasing eye candy. Every inch of set designer Courtney O’Neill’s set has mid-century flair, from the sun-colored kitchen to the texture of the upholstery. And Christine Pascual’s costumes have a big role to play here, especially since Moe chooses to have the very poised and likable Kaplan change them onstage between scenes.</p><p>This retro-fantasy of a world indeed comes off as a legitimate time capsule. entries.title: Rod Blagojevich writes about life in prison, and the hazy conspiracies he believes put him there
entries.summary: <p>Maybe you have a low opinion of former Illinois Gov. Rod Blagojevich. Maybe you blame him for trying to sell the U.S. Senate seat left open by the election of Barack Obama as president in 2008. Maybe you didn't care for Blagojevich <i>before</i> he tried to squeeze money out of a children's hospital.</p><p>Be prepared to change your mind, maybe. Early in his new prison memoir, Blagojevich trots out a character witness.</p><p>"He was set up," President Donald Trump says. "By a lot of bad people. Some of the same people that I had to deal with ... It was sort of a terrible injustice."</p><p>Say no more, right?</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-500000" name="module-500000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>"Well golly," you exclaim, "if Donald Trump thinks he's OK" — and Trump did pardon him — "that's good enough for me!"</p><p>Or maybe, like me, you think, "If Donald Trump is your main character witness, you're really a slimeball."</p><p>Either way, do I have a book for you.</p><p>"Framed F*cked & Freed: A Governor's Odyssey" (Skyhorse: $32.99) — the asterisk is his — is actually two books.</p><p>The first is Blagojevich's spin on the criminal case that saw him sentenced to 14 years in prison. The governor must fill a vacant senate seat. Blagojevich rubs his hands together and says, into an FBI wiretap, "I've got this thing and it's f—ing golden, and I'm not giving it up."</p><p>His attempt to reap personal benefit — plus threatening to withhold grant money to Children's Memorial Hospital unless they cut his campaign fund a check — are dismissed as typical political horse trading.</p><p>Blagojevich insists, repeatedly, that if only all the hours of wiretap tapes were played in court, his innocence would be established. Which is like a mugger saying that if only all the passersby that he <i>didn't </i>rob could be made to testify, he would be a free man.</p><p>He doesn't understand that if after you explain, "OK, you drive the getaway car, and I'll run into the bank and shout, 'Stick 'em up!'" it does not matter if, later, you add that whatever happens in the bank must be "legal, obviously" — words Blagojevich considers exculpatory.</p><p>The former governor — spoiler alert — never grasps what he did wrong. Instead, he floats several hazy conspiracy theories to explain his prosecution, starting with Bank of America, because he forced it to create a workers compensation fund of — and this should really be said aloud, in he voice of Dr. Evil from "Austin Powers" — $1.75 <i>million</i> . Or Barack Obama. Or Patrick Fitzgerald. Or anybody other than himself.</p><p>That said, the middle of "Framed" is an engaging book about nearly eight years in federal prison. The loss of dignity and personal autonomy, horrible food, and how racism and gangs dominate prison life. Blagojevich offers sharp capsule portraits of his fellow cons and has an eye for detail — when a prisoner collapses and dies, guards handcuff and shackle the corpse before transportation.</p><p>He comes so close. Self-realization hovers, tantalizingly, just beyond his grasp.</p><p>Blagojevich describes at length the dishonesty of his fellow felons. "Prison taught me to be suspicious of the stories men told about themselves ... Prison is filled with men who are not what they claim to be ... They could have told themselves: I am here because I cheated people. Perhaps I should stop cheating people ... Their stories allowed them to escape the humiliations of the present ... He understood the easiest way to con me. Talk about your children."</p><p>Blagojevich works his fatherless children like a bellows to stoke sympathy.</p><p>The reader waits for it to finally dawn on him. "And I myself am one of these," to quote Dante.</p><p>Spoiler alert — never happens. He is a victim of "the biggest political hit job in American history." Not once does Blagojevich consider the possibility he might deserve blame for the crimes that a grand jury of ordinary citizens indicted him for and a jury of his peers found him guilty of committing. Instead, self pity and the most elaborate contortions obscure the truth: He sent himself to prison and then kept himself there by his refusal to take responsibility.</p><p>Some of his deceptions are of omission. Again and again, he mentions his early humble manual labor jobs, his hardworking parents. He never whispers the name of his father-in-law, powerful Ald. Dick Mell (33rd) who handed him his political career wrapped in a bow. Never mentions Children's Memorial Hospital, painting his shakedown as "requests for campaign contributions." He seems to think his seeking political donations for conducting state business isn't the same as demanding envelopes of cash.</p><p>Reading Blagojevich's book, I shared one puzzlement with my wife.</p><p>"I'm trying to figure out if he's dishonest or just stupid," I said.</p><p>"Why couldn't he be both?" she replied.</p><p>Bingo.</p>

entries.title: Woman shot in head, 3 others wounded in Englewood shooting
entries.summary: <p>A woman was in serious condition after being shot in the head early Sunday in Englewood that injured three other people, Chicago police said.</p><p>The woman, who responding officers estimated to be about 20, was at a party in the 7200 block of South Green Street when gunshots were heard about 2:04 a.m., police said.</p><p>Chicago Fire Department personnel treated the woman at the scene and took her to the University of Chicago Medical Center in serious condition.</p><p>Three additional victims took themselves to Holy Cross Hospital for treatment, police said.</p><p>A 16-year-old boy was shot in the thigh, an 18-year-old man suffered a gunshot wound to each hand, and another 18-year-old man was shot in the leg. Police said all three were in good condition.</p><p>Area One detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Michael O'Brien's Super 25 high school football rankings for Week 15
entries.summary: <p>One of the silliest things in Illinois high school sports is watching teams that play in the same conference all season compete for different state championships.</p><p>That’s on full display in this year’s state championship football games. CCL Blue rivals Brother Rice (7A) and Mount Carmel (8A) play in different title games on Saturday. CCL Orange conference mates Providence (5A) and Fenwick (6A) will do the same.</p><p>This competitive balance issue isn’t discussed enough and encompasses private and public schools across multiple sports.</p><p>Marshall, a Public League Red West team, won the Class 1A basketball state title last season after competing in a conference with 4A and 3A schools. Orr won three consecutive 2A basketball state titles from 2017-2019 while facing 4A teams in the Red West during the regular season.</p><p>IC Catholic’s football team spends the regular season in the CCL White, facing Joliet Catholic (6A), St. Laurence (7A), and DePaul Prep (8A). This weekend they will face St. Joseph-Ogden in the Class 3A title game.</p><p>Schools can decide which conferences they want to join and who they play in the regular season. That should be factored into the school’s playoff class. It’s a much more reliable indicator of competitive ability than enrollment.</p><h3>Tim Racki chases the record</h3><p>Nazareth opened at No. 5 in the preseason rankings. The Roadrunners, likely behind only Mount Carmel and Brother Rice in terms of college talent, battled injuries all season. They lost four of their first six games, all to good teams: IC Catholic, Mount Carmel, Montini and St. Francis.</p><p>As usual, coach Tim Racki weathered the storm and got his team back on track. Nazareth dominated its first four playoff games, then beat Wheaton-Warrenville South 14-7 in the 6A semifinals.</p><p>Up next is Fenwick in the championship game. Racki has won six titles at Nazareth and won four as Driscoll’s head coach in the early 2000s. He can tie legendary Mount Carmel coach Frank Lenti’s record of 11 championships with a win this weekend.</p><h3>New Trier’s magical run</h3><p>It’s a little strange to see New Trier playing for a state championship in football, even for New Trier. Coach Brian Doll and his players have been fun to talk with throughout the playoff run. They didn’t expect this and have savored every win and special moment.</p><p>The school has played football for 100 years, and this is just the second state championship appearance. The Trevians lost the 6A title game (then the largest class) to Reavis in 1982.</p><p>Purdue recruit Jackie Ryder is the catalyst for New Trier. He threw for 245 yards and accounted for five touchdowns in the Trevians’ semifinal win against St. Ignatius.</p><p>“It is just this group,” Doll said after beating Homewood-Flossmoor in the playoffs. “They have kind of enjoyed it from freshman year on. The seniors are really tight and great leaders.”</p><h3>The stars will play at ISU</h3><p>The state championship games are loaded with Player of the Year contenders. Hersey quarterback Jake Nawrot, who has thrown no interceptions this season, will take on Brother Rice’s dominant defense, led by Kam McGee. Fenwick’s two-way standout Jake Thies returns to the site of his breakout game in last season's state championship.</p><p>Mount Carmel quarterback Brady Cloherty, who has thrown a school record 50 touchdown passes this season, and Caravan receiver Marshaun Thornton are also on the list of contenders.</p><h3>Super 25 high school football rankings for Week 15</h3><p>With record and last week's ranking</p><p><b>1. entries.title: Bears-Saints inactives: receiver/returner Zavion Thomas will play
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> rookie kick returner Zavion Thomas will play Sunday against the Saints after hurting his ankle during the week.</p><p>The team called him questionable on Friday but he was not among the team's inactives. He was the most notable Bears player ruled out for the Saints game at Soldier Field. The other Bears' inactives were third-string quarterback Case Keenum, cornerback Kyler Gordon, linebacker Keyshaun Elliott, offensive tackle Jordan McFadden and defensive lineman Jayden Loving.</p><p>Gordon was ruled out Friday with a shoulder problem. Everyone else is a healthy scratch.</p><p>Thomas ranks seventh in the NFL with 715 kick return yards. In the Bears' last game, he was flagged for a personal foul at the 4-yard line that moved the Bears backward — and Caleb Williams then threw an interception. The Bears didn't play him on offense the rest of the game.</p><p>The Bears and Saints kick off at noon.</p>
